papers.title: DWPP: Dynamic Window Pure Pursuit Considering Velocity and Acceleration Constraints
papers.relevance: Closest prior work to our PP-nominal DWA arbitration: picks the point in the dynamic window nearest the line omega = kappa*v. Ours generalizes with obstacle + nominal-deviation costs.

papers.title: Reachability-Aware Time Scaling for Path Tracking

baseline_summary: Baseline = Pure Pursuit on the diff-drive axle midpoint (unicycle model, wheel speeds w_R,L = (v +/- w d/2)/r with d=0.36 m, r=0.0825 m; joint limit must be >= 28 rad/s to allow v=2.0 and w=1.5 simultaneously). Geometry: lookahead point G=(x_g,y_g) at distance L gives curvature kappa = 2 y_g / L^2 = 2 sin(alpha)/L and w = v*kappa (identical to Nav2 RPP, verified in Humble source). Proposition 1: on a circular path PP has zero steady-state error for any L < 2R (proof in brief), so corner cutting is purely a transient at curvature changes. Proposition 2: linearized error dynamics on a straight path are e'' + (2v/L) e' + (2v^2/L^2) e = 0, i.e. zeta = 1/sqrt(2) for any L and omega_n = sqrt(2) v/L; hence velocity-scaled lookahead L = v*t_L makes the closed-loop poles speed-invariant (theoretical justification for RPP's lookahead_time) and PP's damping cannot be tuned without an extra gain. Noise-derived lower bound: sigma_w = 2Kv sigma_e / L^2 -> L_min(v) = sqrt(2 K v sigma_e / sigma_w,max) (0.45 m at 0.5 m/s, 0.89 m at 2 m/s with sigma_e = 0.03 m). Stanley (virtual-wheelbase mapping w = v tan(delta)/l) has speed-dependent damping (v/l + k), so PP is preferred as base for 0-2 m/s; Stanley kept as ablation. CTE: signed perpendicular distance from GT position to the nearest path segment, segments classified curve if |kappa| > 0.1 1/m plus 0.5 m transition buffer; report mean |e| (spec), RMSE, max, P95. PID: torque->velocity plant derived as decoupled first-order systems (M_v = m + 2J_w/r^2) v' = (tau_L+tau_R)/r - b_v v and (I_z + J_w d^2/(2r^2)) w' = (tau_R-tau_L) d/(2r) - b_w w; PI by pole placement K_p = (2 zeta w_c M_v - b_v) r, K_i = w_c^2 M_v r (~45 N*s, ~137 N at w_c = 6 rad/s, 46 kg), back-calculation anti-windup, 100 Hz, payload-mass gain scheduling; Ziegler-Nichols/relay only as an auxiliary delay-identification step (explicitly inappropriate for a pure first-order plant). S-curve: 7-segment times, closed-form jerk-aware stopping distance D_stop = v^2/(2a) + v a/(2j) and its inverse v_stop(D); online 3rd-order bang-bang filter guaranteeing |a| <= a_max, |j| <= j_max; lateral jerk bound |w'| <= (j_lat,max - |v' w|)/v. Verified stack facts: nav2_core::Controller API (computeVelocityCommands returns TwistStamped, setSpeedLimit), controller_server publishes geometry_msgs/Twist on cmd_vel at 20 Hz, nav2_velocity_smoother limits acceleration only (no jerk), Humble RPP lacks use_fixed_curvature_lookahead, Gazebo Fortress has DiffDrive (with jerk params), JointController, ApplyJointForce (/model/{m}/joint/{j}/cmd_force, Double) and JointStatePublisher systems; ros_gz_bridge maps Float64<->Double and JointState<->Model; TEB is not installed.

proposals.name: CC-PP: Chord-Corrected Pure Pursuit (module 1 of CCRP)
proposals.idea: Split the lookahead chord's lateral coordinate y_g into the part that exists even under perfect tracking (y_g^0, computed from the path in the Frenet frame at the robot's projection) and the true error part; feed forward the local path curvature and feed back only the error part: w = v [ kappa(s_r) + K * 2 (y_g - y_g^0) / L^2 ], with L = clamp(v t_L, L_min(v), L_max) where L_min(v) = sqrt(2 K v sigma_e / sigma_w,max) is derived from localization-noise amplification. Properties proven in the brief: identical to PP on straight lines and circles (K=1); exact geometric tracking of any C^1 path when e = psi = 0; linearized error dynamics are path-invariant with zeta = sqrt(K/2), omega_n = sqrt(2K) v / L, so a single gain K sets damping independent of speed and curvature.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Stanley curvature feedforward (Hoffmann 2007), Kanayama 1990 FF+FB tracking; recent PP/Stanley hybrids (Jung 2025 IMM blend; Lombard 2026 control-point blending); Nav2 RPP (Macenski 2023) and DWPP (Ohnishi 2026) have no such correction.
proposals.expected_gain: Removes PP corner-cutting at straight-to-arc transitions (transient error ~ L^2 kappa / 8 at L = 1.6 m, R = 1.5 m is ~0.2 m for plain PP) so curve-segment mean CTE should drop from >10 cm to the 3-6 cm range while straight-segment behavior is unchanged; one interpretable gain instead of lookahead re-tuning per speed.
proposals.risks: Curvature feedforward needs a smooth (ideally G2) path from the global planner; noisy kappa(s_r) injects omega jumps (mitigated by 0.5 m curvature smoothing and the alpha_max / lateral-jerk rate limit). Exact tracking at curvature steps is impossible under finite omega-dot, so the JRG curvature-rate speed cap must be active. Benefit vanishes on purely straight/circular test paths, so evaluation must include polyline-smoothed A* paths.
proposals.realtime_budget: O(window ~ 40 points) projection + O(1) law per 20 Hz cycle (< 0.05 ms); O(N ~ 2000) curvature preprocessing at setPlan (< 0.2 ms).

proposals.name: JRG: Jerk-bounded Regulated Governor (module 2 of CCRP)
proposals.idea: Arc-length-parametrized speed cap v_cap(s) = min{ v_max, sqrt(a_lat,max/|kappa|), w_max/|kappa|, sqrt(alpha_max/|kappa'|), (j_lat,max/|kappa'|)^(1/3), v_stop(s_goal - s), v_ext } with forward (accel) and backward (jerk-aware stopping distance) passes at setPlan, online v_ref = min(v_b(s_r), v_cte(e), v_ttc), plus a 100 Hz third-order (jerk-limited) online filter in a separate amr_velocity_governor node that replaces nav2_velocity_smoother; E-stop bypasses the jerk limit. Produces ETA = sum(ds / v_bar) for the spec's 15% travel-time prediction metric.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Nav2 RPP curvature/approach regulation (Macenski 2023); Macfarlane-Croft 2003 jerk-bounded S-curve; Kiemel-Kroger ICRA 2024 jerk-limited path traversal; Gholampour-Beaver 2026 reachability-aware time scaling; Arslan 2022 time governors.
proposals.expected_gain: Peak longitudinal jerk bounded at 2 m/s^3 (P99) versus unbounded steps with nav2_velocity_smoother; lateral acceleration <= 0.8 m/s^2 on curves; goal-approach without the RPP linear heuristic; travel-time prediction error within 15% because the same profile is used for prediction and execution.
proposals.risks: Jerk filter adds up to a_max/j_max = 0.5 s lag, lengthening stopping distance (2.5 m from 2 m/s) so DWA admissibility and the safety zones (warning 1.0 m -> <= 0.5 m/s, critical 0.5 m -> <= 0.2 m/s) must use the jerk-aware D_stop; over-conservative kappa' caps if the planner path is not curvature-continuous; the physical payload slip/tip limits (3-12 m/s^2) are not binding at a_max = 1, so the jerk benefit must be reported as vibration/peak reduction, not slip prevention.
proposals.realtime_budget: O(N) at setPlan (< 0.2 ms); O(1) per 20 Hz cycle; O(1) per 100 Hz filter tick.

proposals.name: PP-nominal DWA arbitration (module 3 of CCRP): single owner of cmd_vel
proposals.idea: One nav2_core::Controller plugin (amr_navigation::TrackingController). CC-PP produces the nominal (v*, w*); the team's own DWA core searches the dynamic window with cost J = w_o C_obs + w_t [((v-v*)/v_max)^2 + ((w-w*)/w_max)^2] + w_c C_clear 1[d_min < d_c], with the nominal point itself included in the sample set. Lemma: if the nominal is collision-free and clear, argmin J = (v*, w*), so tracking is exactly CC-PP in free corridors and DWA only deviates near obstacles. Topic chain: controller_server(20 Hz, Twist) -> amr_velocity_governor(100 Hz) -> collision_monitor -> wheel_velocity_pid(100 Hz, ApplyJointForce torques). A standalone DWA plugin is also built for the spec's DWA-vs-TEB comparison (selectable via BT ControllerSelector).
proposals.closest_prior_work: DWPP (Ohnishi & Takahashi 2026: nearest window point to omega = kappa v), Nav2 DWB PathAlign/PathDist critics, Simplex-architecture arbitration (Jager 2025).
proposals.expected_gain: Resolves the spec's dual requirement (own DWA + own PP/Stanley) without two competing cmd_vel publishers; free-corridor CTE equal to CC-PP, obstacle avoidance equal to DWA; smooth transitions because the window is centered on the current velocity and the nominal respects accel limits.
proposals.risks: Grid resolution may miss the nominal unless it is explicitly inserted; weight tuning (w_t vs w_o) affects how early avoidance begins; DWA horizon must include the jerk-filter lag; two-plugin (BT selector) fallback adds switching transients.
proposals.realtime_budget: DWA 11 x 21 samples x 20 steps with footprint checks ~ 1-2 ms per 20 Hz cycle; total plugin ~ 2-3 ms; 5 robots ~ 0.3 CPU core.

proposals.name: Payload-scheduled wheel PI on torque-level Gazebo interface (supporting module)
proposals.idea: Use Gazebo ApplyJointForce (cmd_force per wheel) + JointStatePublisher instead of the DiffDrive system so the team's 100 Hz PI loop (pole-placement gains from the derived first-order plant, back-calculation anti-windup) actually closes on a mass-dependent plant; recompute K_p, K_i from the payload mass published by the task system (45 -> 70 kg would otherwise cut bandwidth 35%).
proposals.closest_prior_work: Standard control practice; Alwala 2026 adaptive neural control is the learning-based alternative.
proposals.expected_gain: Makes the spec's 'PID velocity controller with documented tuning' and 'payload mass reflected in dynamics' requirements verifiable; constant 6 rad/s velocity-loop bandwidth across payloads; step overshoot < 5%, settling < 0.5 s.
proposals.risks: Depends on the simulation team adopting ApplyJointForce/DetachableJoint payload modeling; torque saturation must be set above the a_max requirement so acceleration limiting stays with the S-curve reference; simulation friction/damping (b_v, b_w) must be identified from step tests.

proposals.name: Optional: rollout-based lookahead/gain selection (stretch, ablation only)
proposals.idea: Each cycle evaluate 8 candidate (L, K) pairs by a 1.5 s forward simulation of the CC-PP closed loop on the known path, cost sum e^2 + lambda sum (delta w)^2, low-pass the winner.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Sukhil & Behl 2021 (offline greedy per-waypoint lookahead), Elgouhary & El-Wakeel 2026 (RL lookahead/gain).
proposals.expected_gain: Possible further CTE reduction at transitions when curvature feedforward is imperfect; deterministic and explainable unlike RL.
proposals.risks: Marginal benefit once chord correction is active; parameter chattering without filtering; only pursued if W4 schedule allows.
proposals.realtime_budget: 8 x 15 = 120 unicycle integrations per 20 Hz cycle (< 0.1 ms).

evaluation_plan: Metrics mapped to spec: (1) CTE straight mean |e| <= 5 cm and curve <= 10 cm against Gazebo ground-truth pose (PosePublisher), logged at 20 Hz as [timestamp, planned_x/y, actual_x/y, cte] with automatic straight/curve classification (|kappa| > 0.1 1/m plus 0.5 m transition buffer), plus RMSE/max/P95; (2) jerk from IMU a_x (100 Hz, Savitzky-Golay 11-point) and lateral jerk d(v w)/dt, P99 <= 2 m/s^3; |a| P99 <= 1.0 m/s^2, |alpha| <= 2.0 rad/s^2; (3) travel-time prediction error |T_pred - T_real|/T_real <= 15% using the JRG ETA; (4) response time command-stamp to first motion <= 200 ms (chain budget 50+10+10 ms + physics); (5) CPU <= 80% with 5 robots, per-cycle plugin timing logged; (6) gain-tuning documentation per spec 4.5 with the five-step procedure across three payloads. Scenarios (20 runs each, fixed dynamic-obstacle seeds): S1 30 m straight corridor at 2.0 m/s; S2 aisle-change U-turns R in {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} m; S3 slalom; S4 three consecutive 90-degree intersections; S5 payload 0/10/25 kg; S6 GT vs EKF pose input (separates tracker error from localization error); S7 1.0 m/s crossing dynamic obstacle (DWA intervention; deviation <= 1 m, recovery <= 5 s per spec 4.7). Baselines: Nav2 RPP (Humble defaults and a re-tuned set for 2 m/s), DWB (Nav2 DWA), MPPI (installed), TEB (source build, open question), team plain PP (K=1, no correction), Stanley virtual-wheelbase. Ablations: chord correction on/off, velocity-scaled lookahead on/off, K in {1, 1.5, 2}, jerk filter on/off, CTE slowdown on/off, rollout lookahead. Statistics: mean +/- std, paired Wilcoxon on shared seeds, success rate, zero collisions, minimum clearance. Report to docs/reports/path_tracking_eval.md.
implementation_plan: Language: C++17 for the nav2_core plugins and the two 100 Hz nodes (plugins must be C++); a ROS-independent core library (amr_tracking_core) so gtest runs without ROS; Python 3.10 for evaluation/logging and a numpy reference implementation used to cross-check the C++ core. Package src/amr_navigation (currently a Python-only skeleton; package.xml already declares nav2_core/nav2_costmap_2d/pluginlib-family deps): include/amr_navigation/tracking/{path_geometry, pure_pursuit, speed_governor, jerk_filter, dwa_core, tracking_controller}.hpp, src/tracking/*.cpp, src/plugins/{tracking_controller, dwa_controller}.cpp, src/nodes/{velocity_governor_node, wheel_velocity_pid_node}.cpp, amr_navigation/eval/{cte_logger, jerk_metrics, eta_metrics}.py, plugins/amr_controllers.xml (pluginlib base nav2_core::Controller), config/{tracking_controller, wheel_pid, velocity_governor}.yaml, test/{test_path_geometry, test_pure_pursuit, test_speed_governor, test_jerk_filter, test_wheel_pid}.cpp + test_cte_metrics.py. CMake: add_library(amr_tracking_core SHARED), add_library(amr_controllers SHARED) with ament_target_dependencies(rclcpp rclcpp_lifecycle nav2_core nav2_costmap_2d nav2_util nav_2d_utils pluginlib tf2_geometry_msgs angles) and pluginlib_export_plugin_description_file(nav2_core plugins/amr_controllers.xml), two add_executable nodes, five ament_add_gtest; add angles, nav2_util, nav_2d_utils, pluginlib, tf2_geometry_msgs, sensor_msgs, std_msgs to package.xml; keep -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic warning-free. ROS interfaces (per /amr_i namespace): controller_server FollowPath plugin amr_navigation::TrackingController (params lookahead_time 0.8, min/max lookahead 0.4/1.8, damping_gain_K 1.0, sigma_e 0.04, sigma_omega_max 0.15, max vel/accel/jerk from robot_params, max_lateral_accel 0.8, max_lateral_jerk 1.5, cte_slowdown [0.05, 0.30], dwa {11x21 samples, 1.0 s, weights}) and FollowPathDWA amr_navigation::DWAController; cmd_vel (Twist, 20 Hz) -> amr_velocity_governor -> cmd_vel_smoothed -> nav2_collision_monitor -> cmd_vel_safe -> wheel_velocity_pid -> /model/amr_i/joint/{left,right}_wheel_joint/cmd_force (std_msgs/Float64 bridged to ignition.msgs.Double); feedback JointState via JointStatePublisher (ignition.msgs.Model); payload_mass (Float64) subscription for gain scheduling; nav2_msgs/SpeedLimit honored through setSpeedLimit -> v_ext; E-stop bypass service on the governor. Gazebo-side requests to the simulation team: ApplyJointForce on both wheel joints, JointStatePublisher, PosePublisher for GT, DetachableJoint payload models. Unit tests: PP curvature exact on circles (<1e-9), zero feedback under perfect tracking (line/circle/clothoid), 4.3% overshoot at K=1 and none at K=2, jerk filter bounds and 2.5 s 0->2 m/s time, v_stop(D_stop(v)) identity, PI anti-windup overshoot < 5%, forward/backward pass monotonicity, nominal-inclusive DWA returns the nominal in free space, CTE logger sign/segmentation. Compute budget: ~2-3 ms per 20 Hz cycle per robot (DWA dominant), 5 robots ~0.3 core; 100 Hz nodes negligible. Schedule: W1 core geometry/CC-PP/governor + gtest + numpy cross-check; W2 plugin, wheel PID, bridge, single-robot driving; W3 DWA integration, scenario automation, logging; W4 baselines (RPP/DWB/MPPI/TEB), payload runs, report and peer-review doc docs/algorithms/path_tracking.md.
open_questions: CTE reference: the spec measures planned path vs actual (ground-truth) trajectory, and its 5 cm straight-line localization tolerance equals the CTE tolerance; we budget 2 cm for the tracker itself, but if EKF bias pushes GT-based CTE over 5 cm we need agreement on also reporting estimated-pose-based CTE.

TEB baseline: teb_local_planner is not in the image and has no official Humble binary (community ros2 branches); the source branch/commit must be agreed with the local-planning owner, or MPPI (installed) reported as an additional baseline.

Wheel actuation choice in Gazebo: ApplyJointForce (torque, our PID) versus the DiffDrive system (plugin-internal velocity control). This brief assumes the former; it determines whether the spec's PID requirement and payload-mass dynamics are meaningful.

Curvature continuity of the global planner's smoothed path (G2 spline/clothoid vs polyline): large kappa' would make the JRG curvature-rate caps over-conservative and make curvature feedforward noisy.
Ordering and naming of the cmd_vel chain with the safety system: collision_monitor placement after the jerk governor and the E-stop bypass service must be fixed with the safety-system owner.
Definition of the 15% travel-time prediction metric (prediction at plan time vs updated after replanning) to be agreed with the planner team.
Mechanism for runtime payload mass change in Gazebo Fortress (DetachableJoint payload model vs inertial component edit) and the payload_mass topic contract with the task/behavior team.
